concepts.title: Place Value to Thousandths & Powers of 10
know: Each place in a number is worth 10 times the place to its right, and {{1/10}} of the place to its left.
Multiplying by 10 shifts every digit one place to the left (the number gets 10 times bigger).
Dividing by 10 shifts every digit one place to the right (each digit is worth {{1/10}} as much).
A power of 10 like 10<sup>3</sup> means 10 × 10 × 10 = 1,000 — the exponent tells you how many 10s are multiplied.
When you multiply or divide by 10<sup>n</sup>, the digits shift n places.

mc.q: In the number 55.5, how does the value of the 5 in the tens place compare to the value of the 5 in the ones place?
mc.explain: The tens-place 5 is worth 50 and the ones-place 5 is worth 5, and 50 = 10 × 5. It is not 100 times as great — that compares places two apart, not neighbors.

mc.q: What is 3.7 × 10?
mc.explain: Multiplying by 10 shifts each digit one place left: 3.7 becomes 37. Writing 3.70 just adds a zero without changing the value, and 0.37 shifts the wrong direction.

mc.q: What is the value of 10<sup>3</sup>?
mc.explain: 10<sup>3</sup> means 10 × 10 × 10 = 1,000. It does not mean 10 × 3 = 30, and 10,000 would be 10<sup>4</sup>.

mc.q: What is 45.6 ÷ 100?
mc.explain: Dividing by 100 shifts the digits two places right: 45.6 → 4.56 → 0.456. Choosing 4.56 only shifts one place, and 4,560 multiplies instead of divides.

mc.q: In 0.777, the 7 in the tenths place is worth how many times the 7 in the hundredths place?
mc.explain: The tenths 7 is worth 0.7 and the hundredths 7 is worth 0.07, and 0.7 = 10 × 0.07. It is not {{1/10}} as much — that describes moving right, not left.

mc.q: What is 0.83 × 10<sup>2</sup>?
mc.explain: 10<sup>2</sup> = 100, so shift the digits two places left: 0.83 becomes 83. Picking 8.3 shifts only one place; 0.0083 divides instead of multiplies.

mc.q: A juice company packs 6.04 liters into each crate. How many liters are in 1,000 crates? (Find 6.04 × 1,000.)
mc.explain: Multiplying by 1,000 shifts the digits three places left: 6.04 → 6,040. Just tacking on zeros to get 6.04000 does not change the value at all.

mc.q: Which expression is equal to 700?
mc.explain: 7 × 10<sup>2</sup> = 7 × 100 = 700. The exponent counts the 10s, so 7 × 10<sup>3</sup> = 7,000 — too big by one shift.

mc.q: Jaden divided 3,500 by a power of 10 and got 3.5. What power of 10 did he divide by?
mc.explain: The digits shifted three places right (3,500 → 350 → 35 → 3.5), so he divided by 10<sup>3</sup> = 1,000. Dividing by 10<sup>2</sup> would give 35, not 3.5.

mc.q: In which number does the digit 4 have a value that is 100 times the value of the 4 in 0.048?
mc.explain: In 0.048 the 4 is worth 0.04, and 100 × 0.04 = 4, so we need a 4 in the ones place: 34.5. In 542 the 4 is worth 40, which is 1,000 times as much.

open.solution: Count the number of 10s being multiplied: there are four. The exponent tells how many 10s, so 10 × 10 × 10 × 10 = 10<sup>4</sup>, which equals 10,000.
Multiplying by 100 shifts every digit two places to the left. 7.03 → 70.3 → 703. So 7.03 × 100 = 703.
10<sup>3</sup> = 1,000, so shift the digits three places to the right. 96 → 9.6 → 0.96 → 0.096. So 96 ÷ 10<sup>3</sup> = 0.096.

open.q: A dime is worth {{1/10}} of a dollar. Amara saved 1,000 dimes in a jar. How many dollars does she have?
open.solution: Each dime is worth $0.10. Multiply: 1,000 × 0.10 shifts the digits of 0.10 three places left, giving 100. Amara has $100.

open.q: The value of the 6 in 63,000 is how many times the value of the 6 in 630?
open.solution: In 63,000 the 6 is worth 60,000. In 630 the 6 is worth 600. Divide: 60,000 ÷ 600 = 100. The 6 moved two places left, and each place is worth 10 times more, so 10 × 10 = 100 times.

challenge.q: A number machine multiplies whatever you put in by 10, then by 10 again, then by 10 a third time, and finally divides the result by 100. Zoe puts in a mystery number and 4.5 comes out. What number did Zoe put in?
challenge.solution: Multiplying by 10 three times is the same as multiplying by 10<sup>3</sup> = 1,000. Then dividing by 100 undoes two of those shifts, so overall the machine just multiplies by 1,000 ÷ 100 = 10. If the output is 4.5, the input must be 4.5 ÷ 10 = 0.45. Check: 0.45 × 1,000 = 450, and 450 ÷ 100 = 4.5. ✓

concepts.title: Reading, Writing, Comparing & Rounding Decimals
know: Read a decimal by saying the whole part, "and" for the decimal point, then the decimal part with its last place name: 8.309 is "eight and three hundred nine thousandths".
Expanded form shows each digit times its place value, like 40.73 = 4×10 + 7×{{1/10}} + 3×{{1/100}}.
To compare decimals, line up the decimal points and compare place by place from the left. You can add zeros on the end: 0.9 = 0.90.
A longer decimal is NOT automatically bigger — 0.4 is greater than 0.35.
To round, find the rounding place, look at the digit just to its right: 5 or more rounds up, 4 or less keeps the digit the same.

mc.q: Which numeral means "six and three tenths"?
mc.explain: "Six and three tenths" is 6 wholes plus 3 in the tenths place: 6.3. Writing 6.03 puts the 3 in the hundredths place instead.

mc.q: Which number is the greatest?
mc.explain: Compare tenths first: 0.1 has 1 tenth while the others have 0 tenths, so 0.1 is greatest. More digits does not mean bigger — 0.089 is less than 0.1.

mc.q: Round 3.86 to the nearest tenth.
mc.explain: The tenths digit is 8; the digit to its right is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up to 3.9. Choosing 3.8 forgets to round up; 4 rounds to the nearest whole instead.

mc.q: Which is the expanded form of 40.73?
mc.explain: The 4 is 4 tens, the 7 is 7 tenths, and the 3 is 3 hundredths: 40 + 0.7 + 0.03 = 40.73. The first choice equals 47.3 — a place-value slip.

mc.q: Which numeral means "twelve and forty-six thousandths"?
mc.explain: Forty-six thousandths must end in the thousandths place, so write 046 after the point: 12.046. Writing 12.46 says forty-six hundredths instead.

mc.q: Which list shows 2.5, 2.35, 2.53, and 2.05 in order from least to greatest?
mc.explain: Write them as 2.50, 2.35, 2.53, 2.05 and compare: 2.05 < 2.35 < 2.50 < 2.53. Remember 2.5 = 2.50, which is more than 2.35, not less.

mc.q: A puppy weighs 82.462 pounds... just kidding — a baby hippo does! Round 82.462 to the nearest tenth.
mc.explain: The tenths digit is 4; the hundredths digit is 6, which is 5 or more, so round up to 82.5. Choosing 82.46 rounds to the hundredth, not the tenth.

mc.q: Which number rounds to 6.4 when rounded to the nearest tenth?
mc.explain: 6.44 has a 4 in the hundredths place, so it rounds down to 6.4. But 6.45 rounds up to 6.5, and 6.349 rounds to 6.3.

mc.q: Which comparison is true?
mc.explain: Write 0.78 as 0.780; comparing hundredths, 0 < 8, so 0.708 < 0.78. Don't compare digit counts — 708 looks bigger than 78, but place value says otherwise, and 0.5 = 0.50 exactly.

mc.q: Nora's number, rounded to the nearest whole number, is 15. Rounded to the nearest tenth, it is 14.6. Which could be Nora's number?
mc.explain: 14.64 rounds to 14.6 (the 4 hundredths round down) and to 15 (the 6 tenths round up) — both clues fit. 14.66 fails because it rounds to 14.7.

open.answer: Eight and three hundred nine thousandths
open.solution: The whole part is 8, so say "eight and". The decimal part 309 ends in the thousandths place, so read it as "three hundred nine thousandths". Together: eight and three hundred nine thousandths.
The 5 is 5 hundreds, the 0 tens adds nothing, the 7 is 7 ones, the 2 is 2 tenths, and the 6 is 6 hundredths. So 507.26 = 5×100 + 7×1 + 2×{{1/10}} + 6×{{1/100}}.

open.q: Write >, =, or < to make this true: 0.86 ___ 0.9
open.solution: Write 0.9 as 0.90 so both have hundredths. Compare tenths: 8 < 9, so 0.86 < 0.90. The answer is <.

open.q: Four friends ran a 100-meter race. Ava finished in 14.32 seconds, Ben in 14.4 seconds, Cara in 14.23 seconds, and Dev in 14.3 seconds. Who won the race?
open.solution: The winner has the least time. Write the times with hundredths: 14.32, 14.40, 14.23, 14.30. Comparing tenths then hundredths, 14.23 is the smallest, so Cara won.
The tenths digit is 9; the hundredths digit is 5, so round up. Rounding 249.9 up by one tenth gives 250.0, because the 9 tenths becomes 10 tenths and regroups into the ones place.

challenge.q: I am a decimal in the form 0.___ ___ ___ (three decimal places). Rounded to the nearest hundredth, I am 0.35. My thousandths digit is odd, and the sum of my three decimal digits is 12. What number am I?
challenge.solution: To round to 0.35, the number must be from 0.345 up to 0.354. So it is 0.34_ (thousandths 5–9) or 0.35_ (thousandths 0–4). Try 0.34_: the digits 3 + 4 + c = 12 gives c = 5, which is odd and in range — that works! Try 0.35_: 3 + 5 + c = 12 gives c = 4, which is even, so it fails. The number is 0.345.

concepts.title: Prime, Composite & Prime Factorization
know: A prime number has exactly two factors: 1 and itself. Examples: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11.
A composite number has more than two factors. Example: 15 has factors 1, 3, 5, 15.
The number 1 is neither prime nor composite — it has only one factor.
2 is the only even prime number; every other even number is composite.
Prime factorization breaks a composite number into a product of primes, and a factor tree helps you find it: keep splitting until every branch ends in a prime.
Even + even = even, odd + odd = even, and even + odd = odd.

mc.q: Which number is prime?
mc.explain: The only factors of 11 are 1 and 11, so it is prime. Being odd is not enough: 9 = 3 × 3, 15 = 3 × 5, and 21 = 3 × 7 are all composite.

mc.q: Which number is composite?
mc.explain: 27 = 3 × 9, so it has factors besides 1 and itself — composite. The numbers 2, 13, and 31 each have exactly two factors, so they are prime.

mc.q: The number 1 is:
mc.explain: A prime needs exactly two different factors, but 1 has only one factor (itself). So 1 is neither prime nor composite.

mc.q: Which is the prime factorization of 36?
mc.explain: 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 = 36 and every factor is prime. The others equal 36 too, but 4, 9, 18, and 6 are composite, so they are not prime factorizations.

mc.q: Which is the only even prime number?
mc.explain: 2 has exactly two factors, 1 and 2, so it is prime. Every other even number can be divided by 2, so it has extra factors and is composite.

mc.q: Tia starts a factor tree for 45 by splitting it into 9 × 5. What is the complete prime factorization of 45?
mc.explain: The 9 is composite, so keep splitting: 9 = 3 × 3. That gives 45 = 3 × 3 × 5, all primes. Stopping at 9 × 5 leaves a composite factor in the tree.

mc.q: The sum of two odd numbers is always:
mc.explain: Try examples: 3 + 5 = 8 and 7 + 9 = 16 — always even. Each odd number is an even number plus 1, and the two extra 1s pair up to make the sum even.

mc.q: Which number between 90 and 100 is prime?
mc.explain: 97 is not divisible by 2, 3, 5, or 7, so it is prime. The trap is 91: it looks prime but 91 = 7 × 13, and 93 = 3 × 31, 99 = 9 × 11.

mc.q: Amir claims that every odd number greater than 1 is prime. Which number proves he is wrong?
mc.explain: 51 is odd but composite: 51 = 3 × 17, so it breaks Amir's rule. The numbers 23, 41, and 53 are all prime, so they don't disprove him.

mc.q: Which is the prime factorization of 84?
mc.explain: 84 = 2 × 42 = 2 × 2 × 21 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 7, and all of those factors are prime. The other choices equal 84 but still contain composite factors like 14, 4, 21, or 42.

open.q: List all the prime numbers between 20 and 35.
open.solution: Check each number from 21 to 34. Cross out evens and multiples of 3 or 5: 21 = 3×7, 25 = 5×5, 27 = 3×9, 33 = 3×11. Only 23, 29, and 31 have no factors besides 1 and themselves.

open.q: Use a factor tree to find the prime factorization of 60.
open.solution: Split 60 = 6 × 10. Then split 6 = 2 × 3 and 10 = 2 × 5. All branches now end in primes, so 60 = 2 × 2 × 3 × 5. Check: 2 × 2 = 4, 4 × 3 = 12, 12 × 5 = 60. ✓

open.q: Is 87 prime or composite? Explain how you know.
open.solution: Test small primes. 87 is odd, so 2 doesn't work. The digits 8 + 7 = 15, which is divisible by 3, so 87 is divisible by 3: 87 = 3 × 29. Since it has more than two factors, 87 is composite.

open.q: Mr. Ortiz wants to arrange 29 desks into equal rows, with more than one row and more than one desk in each row. Can he do it? Explain.
open.solution: Equal rows means the number of rows times desks per row equals 29. Since 29 is prime, its only factors are 1 and 29, so the only arrangements are 1 row of 29 or 29 rows of 1. Neither fits the rule, so he cannot do it.

open.q: Jo adds an even number to an odd number, then multiplies the sum by 2. Is her final result even or odd?
open.solution: An even plus an odd is always odd (for example, 4 + 3 = 7). Multiplying any whole number by 2 always gives an even number (7 × 2 = 14). So the final result is always even.

challenge.q: Zara's locker number is between 50 and 100. Its prime factorization is exactly three different prime numbers multiplied together, each used only once. One of those primes is 5. What is Zara's locker number?
challenge.solution: The number is 5 × p × q for two different primes p and q (neither equal to 5). So p × q must be between 50 ÷ 5 = 10 and 100 ÷ 5 = 20. Try prime pairs: 2 × 3 = 6 (too small, gives 30), 2 × 7 = 14 (gives 5 × 14 = 70 ✓), 2 × 11 = 22 (too big), 3 × 7 = 21 (too big). Only 70 works: 70 = 2 × 5 × 7.
